Hypochlorous acid: Antoine Jérôme Balard. Hypochlorous acid is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula ClOH, also written as HClO, HOCl, or ClHO.
Who is credited with discovering Gallium?
Gallium: Paul-Émile Lecoq de Boisbaudran. Gallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ga and atomic number 31.
A King's College Cambridge graduate who earned a Princeton doctorate in 1938, he later joined Britain's wartime codebreaking effort and pioneered theoretical computing — who was he?
Alan Turing (23 June 1912 - 7 June 1954) was an English mathematician, computer scientist, logician, cryptanalyst, philosopher and theoretical biologist.
One of Ptolemy's original 48 and among the largest in the sky, this autumn constellation is named for a mythical princess chained to a rock for the sea monster Cetus — which one?
Andromeda (constellation) is one of the 48 constellations listed by the 2nd-century Greco-Roman astronomer Ptolemy, and one of the 88 modern constellations.

In 2003, this American mountaineer amputated his own trapped forearm with a dull pocket knife after five days pinned by a boulder in a Utah canyon, then rappelled and hiked miles to safety — who is he?

Aron Ralston (born October 27, 1975) is an American mountaineer, mechanical engineer, and motivational speaker, known for surviving a canyoneering accident in 2003 by cutting off part of his own right arm.
Which SI unit of radioactivity honors the scientist who co-discovered the phenomenon alongside the Curies?
Becquerel (symbol: Bq) is the unit of radioactivity in the International System of Units (SI).

Native to eastern North America with resident populations as far north as Newfoundland, this crested songbird in the crow family has a black, U-shaped collar around its neck and a mostly white chest — name it?
Blue jay (Cyanocitta cristata) is a passerine bird in the family Corvidae, native to eastern North America.
This flammable, colorless alkane gas with the formula C4H10 takes its name from a Greek word for butter, via butyric acid — what is it?
Butane is an alkane with the formula C4H10. Butane exists as two isomers, n-butane, CH3CH2CH2CH3 and iso-butane, (CH3)3CH.
This root vegetable owes its typical orange color to beta-carotene, though heirloom varieties can be white, purple, or even black — what vegetable is it?
Born in 1847, this American wore three hats at once — psychologist, logician, and mathematician. Who was she?
Christine Ladd-Franklin (December 1, 1847 - March 5, 1930) was an American psychologist, logician, and mathematician.
With algorithms and data structures at its core and the theory of computation among its branches, which field studies computation, information, and automation?

Computer science is the study of computation, information, and automation. The theory of computation concerns abstract models of computation and general classes of problems that can be solved using them.
A law professor known for scholarship on retribution and criminal sentencing, this Harvard-trained academic was killed in 2014 in a murder-for-hire scheme linked to a custody dispute — who is he?

Dan Markel (October 9, 1972 - July 19, 2014) was a Canadian-born attorney and law professor who wrote various works on retribution in criminal law and sentencing with a focus on the role of punishment in the criminal justice system.

England-born but raised in Australia, this geologist did much of his real rock-hunting in the Flinders Ranges — though he's better remembered for braving the ice alongside Shackleton on the Nimrod Expedition; who was he?
Douglas Mawson (5 May 1882 - 14 October 1958) was an Australian geologist, Antarctic explorer, and academic.
This branch of medicine studies the body's hormone-secreting glands and the chemical messengers, called hormones, that regulate growth, metabolism, mood, and more — name the field?
Endocrinology (from endocrine + -ology) is a branch of biology and medicine dealing with the endocrine system, its diseases, and its specific secretions known as hormones.
Every member of this mammal family is an obligate carnivore with retractile claws and a powerful bite, from forest dwellers to desert hunters — which family is it?
Felidae is the family of mammals in the order Carnivora colloquially referred to as cats.
Most common in the hands and feet, this cold-exposure injury can lead to complications like hypothermia or compartment syndrome — what is it called?
Frostbite is an injury to skin or other living tissue that is allowed to freeze, especially affecting the fingers, toes, nose, ears, cheeks and chin.

This small freshwater fish, native to China and one of the world's most popular aquarium pets, has become an invasive pest after being released into wild waterways in North America and Australia — what fish is it?
Goldfish (Carassius auratus) is a freshwater fish in the family Cyprinidae of the order Cypriniformes.
Tapeworms, flukes, and roundworms burrowing into the gut and beyond all fall under this macroparasitic disease — a neglected tropical illness better known as worm infection. What is it?
Helminthiasis is any macroparasitic disease of humans and other animals in which a part of the body is infected with parasitic worms, known as helminths.
Dissolved in water it yields a notoriously corrosive acid, yet it's also the main industrial route to fluorine and a feedstock for Teflon-style polymers like PTFE — which colorless compound is it?
Hydrogen fluoride is an inorganic compound with chemical formula HF.

Acting as the eye's diaphragm in optical terms, this thin ring-shaped structure controls how much light reaches the retina by adjusting the pupil's size, and also determines a person's eye color — name this structure?

Iris (anatomy) (pl.: irides or irises) is a thin, ring-shaped structure in the eye in most mammals and birds that is responsible for controlling the diameter and size of the pupil, and thus the amount of light reaching the retina.

He wrote the first commercial anti-virus software in 1987 and ran twice for the Libertarian presidential nomination — yet later urged people to uninstall the very product that still bears his name. Who is he?
John McAfee (18 September 1945 - 23 June 2021) was a British and American computer programmer, businessman, and two-time U.S.
Endemic to New Zealand, this large, nocturnal, ground-dwelling parrot has owl-like forward-facing eyes and holds the title of the world's only flightless parrot — what bird is it?
Kākāpō (Mori:; pl.: kkp; Strigops habroptilus), sometimes known as the owl-parrot, is a species of large, nocturnal, ground-dwelling parrot of the superfamily Strigopoidea.
Believed to stem from genetic and hormonal disruption of the lymphatic system, this condition traps fat in the legs regardless of a woman's overall weight — what's the diagnosis?
Lipedema is a condition that is almost exclusively found in women and results in enlargement of both legs due to deposits of fat under the skin.
Transmitted by the bite of Anopheles mosquitoes, this infectious disease causes fever, fatigue, and headaches, and in severe cases can lead to seizures, coma, or death — name the disease?
Malaria is a mosquito-borne infectious disease that is transmitted by the bite of Anopheles mosquitoes.
Crushed leaves of this mint-family herb smell like spearmint, yet it has caused deaths when used as a traditional abortifacient — which species, also known as pennyroyal?

Mentha pulegium (European) pennyroyal, or pennyrile, also called mosquito plant and pudding grass, is a species of flowering plant in the mint family, Lamiaceae, native to Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East.
In 1812 Étienne Geoffroy grouped the apes with the Cercopithecidae under the name Catarrhini, or "Old World" members of this familiar simian group — what common name is it?
Monkey is a common name that may refer to most mammals of the infraorder Simiiformes, also known as simians.

Encompassing several types of kidney inflammation affecting the glomeruli, tubules, or nearby interstitial tissue, this general medical term falls under the broader category of nephropathy — what's the condition?
Nephritis is inflammation of the kidneys and may involve the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitial tissue surrounding the glomeruli and tubules.
Concerned with the most fundamental concept of all — being — this branch of metaphysics distinguishes non-repeatable particulars from repeatable universals like 'green' — what is the field?
Ontology is the philosophical study of being.
Named for the extra copy of chromosome 13 found in affected cells, this condition — related to Down and Edwards syndromes — disrupts normal organ development — which syndrome?
Patau syndrome is a syndrome caused by a chromosomal abnormality, in which some or all of the cells of the body contain extra genetic material from chromosome 13.
This anxiety disorder involves an irrational, excessive, and persistent fear of a specific object or situation, often leading sufferers to go to great lengths to avoid it — what is it called?
Phobia is an anxiety disorder, defined by an irrational, unrealistic, persistent and excessive fear of an object or situation.
Named from the Greek for an infinite carbon chain it would ultimately become, this class of organic compounds strings together alternating single and triple bonds. What is it called?
Polyyne is any organic compound with alternating single and triple bonds; that is, a series of consecutive alkynes, (CC)n with n greater than 1.

Brought from China to Europe in the sixteenth century and popularized by the House of Orange in the Netherlands, this dog breed is known for its wrinkly, short-muzzled face and curled tail — name the breed?
Pug is a breed of dog with the physically distinctive features of a wrinkly, short-muzzled face, and curled tail.
Also called king's crown or Arctic root, this Arctic-growing perennial is widely sold as a supplement even though regulators say its health claims lack solid evidence — which plant?
Rhodiola rosea (commonly golden root, rose root, roseroot, Aaron's rod, Arctic root, king's crown, lignum rhodium, orpin rose) is a perennial flowering plant in the family Crassulaceae.
Having taught economics at the Catholic University of Asunción and once served as Paraguay's finance minister, this politician assumed his country's presidency in 2023 — who is he?
Santiago Peña (Spanish; born 16 November 1978) is a Paraguayan politician and economist who has served as the 52nd president of Paraguay since 2023.

Defined by the American Thoracic Society as a subjective, uncomfortable experience of breathing discomfort that can include chest tightness or a sense of effort to breathe — what is this sensation called?
Shortness of breath (SOB), known as dyspnea (in AmE) or dyspnoea (in BrE), is an uncomfortable feeling of not being able to breathe well enough.

Distinguished from relatives in its conifer family by four-sided needles attached singly to small peg-like structures on the twigs, this genus of about 37 evergreen tree species thrives across the Northern Hemisphere's boreal forests — what's the tree?

Spruce is a tree of the genus Picea, a genus of some 37 species of coniferous evergreen trees in the family Pinaceae, found in the northern temperate and boreal (taiga) regions of the Northern Hemisphere.
This Turkish businesswoman served as one of her father's chief advisers back in 2013, when he held the office of prime minister and later became Turkey's president — who is she?
Sümeyye Erdoğan (ne Erdoan; born 22 August 1985) is a Turkish businesswoman and the daughter of President Recep Tayyip Erdoan.
Shaped like a butterfly and located in the neck just below the Adam's apple, this endocrine gland's two lobes are joined by a thin band of tissue called the isthmus — name the gland?

Thyroid is an endocrine gland in vertebrates. The lower two thirds of the lobes are connected by a thin band of tissue called the isthmus (pl.: isthmi). The thyroid gland secretes three hormones: the two thyroid hormones – triiodothyronine (T3) and thyroxine (T4) – and a peptide hormone, calcitonin.

One of the two main forms of inflammatory bowel disease, this long-term condition inflames and ulcerates the colon and rectum, flaring up with abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea before quieting down again — what is it?
Ulcerative colitis (UC) is one of the two types of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), with the other type being Crohn's disease.
Belonging mostly to one family of long-snouted beetles, this group includes bark beetles and grain-damaging pests despite some members lacking the trademark snout — what are they?
Weevil are beetles belonging to the superfamily Curculionoidea, known for their very long snouts.
Also called motor neuron disease or Lou Gehrig's disease, this terminal condition progressively destroys the neurons that control voluntary muscle movement — what is it?
Nicknamed the painted hunter for its mottled coat, this sub-Saharan canine hunts cooperatively at dawn and dusk and is the only living member of its genus, Lycaon — which species?
African wild dog: Species of canine. The African wild dog (Lycaon pictus), also called painted dog and Cape hunting dog, is a wild canine native to sub-Saharan Africa.
Unlike its bulb-forming relative, the common onion, this perennial vegetable never forms a bulb and owes one of its names to its hollow, tube-like leaves — which plant?
Allium fistulosum: Species of plant. The species is very similar in taste and odor to the related common onion, Allium cepa, and hybrids between the two (tree onions) exist.
A branch of morphology with roots in prehistoric times, which natural science studies the internal and external structure of organisms and their parts?
Anatomy: Study of the structure of organisms. Anatomy is a branch of natural science that deals with the structural organization of living things.
Commonly called a canker sore, this recurring condition produces benign mouth ulcers that heal within 7 to 10 days but often return three to six times a year — what is it?
Aphthous stomatitis: Common oral condition lasting 7–10 days.
Originally conceived as the average Earth-Sun distance before its 2012 redefinition, this measure equals about 499 light-seconds and underpins the definition of the parsec — what is it called?
Astronomical unit: Mean distance between Earth and the Sun.

The most widespread bird in its family, found on every continent except Antarctica (where only stray vagrants appear), this species has blue upperparts, a deeply forked tail, and usually nests in man-made structures — what is it?
Barn swallow: Species of bird. The barn swallow (Hirundo rustica) is the most widespread species of swallow in the world, occurring on all continents, with vagrants reported even in Antarctica.
This interdisciplinary field examines moral questions raised by advances in biology, medicine, and biotechnology, touching everything from patient care to environmental policy — what is it called?
Bioethics: Study of the ethical issues emerging from advances in biology and medicine.

Bred in South Africa as a family guard dog, this large mastiff-type breed has a short coat and heavy bone structure, and is recognized by that country's kennel union but not the international federation — what breed is it?
Boerboel: South African breed of dog. The Boerboel (pronounced [ˈbuːrbul]) is a South African breed of large dog of mastiff type, used as a family guard dog.
An intact, more muscular and aggressive adult male of the cattle species, this animal has long been a sacrificial symbol in many religions and stars in famous arena sports. What is it?
Bull: Adult male cattle. A bull is an intact (i.e., not castrated) adult male of the species Bos taurus (cattle).
Also known as hemp when grown for fiber rather than its psychoactive use, this Asian-native plant genus includes up to three disputed species — which plant?
Their young are calves and their castrated males are oxen; this widespread bovid is the most far-flung species of the genus Bos — what animal is it?

One of the earliest cultivated legumes — its oldest traces were unearthed in Syria — this protein-packed seed goes by names like garbanzo and chana, and forms the backbone of hummus and falafel. What is it?
Chickpea: Species of flowering plant with edible seeds.
Sold as Catapres and Kapvay, this drug treats high blood pressure, ADHD, and drug-withdrawal symptoms, and can be delivered via a skin patch — what is it?

Nicknamed the deaf adder or long-cripple in parts of Europe, this legless, burrowing lizard has smooth scales that don't overlap — and despite its name, it's neither a snake nor what it sounds like. What is it?
Common slow worm: Species of legless lizard. The common slow worm (Anguis fragilis) is a non-venomous species of legless lizard native to Europe.
Found in the tropics of Africa, Asia, the Americas, and Australia, this large semiaquatic reptile congregates in rivers and wetlands and is closely related to alligators and caimans — what is it?
Crocodile: Family of large reptilian carnivores.
In 1900, this mathematician presented a list of unsolved problems that shaped 20th-century mathematical research — who is he?
This linguistic term describes a combination of two vowel sounds gliding together within a single syllable, as heard five times in the phrase 'no highway cowboys' — what is it called?

Diphthong: Combination of two adjacent vowel sounds. A diphthong ( DIF-thong, DIP-), also known as a gliding vowel or a vowel glide, is a combination of two adjacent vowel sounds within the same syllable.
Nicknamed the spiny anteater, this quill-covered, egg-laying mammal from Australia and New Guinea has babies called puggles — which creature?

This anaerobic parasite infects tens of millions of people worldwide, causing a gut disease whose name comes from a word meaning tissue disintegration, and kills over 55,000 people each year — what is it?
With a glossy black head and a distinctive white bill shield, this rail-family waterbird is found from Europe to Australia — which bird?
Eurasian coot: Species of bird. The Eurasian coot (Fulica atra), also known as the common coot or Australian coot, is a member of the rail and crake bird family, the Rallidae.

An annual legume with leaves of three small leaflets, this semiarid crop has flavored dishes of the Indian subcontinent since ancient times — yet there's little clinical proof it works as the supplement people often take. What is it?
With a bushy tail, triangular ears, and a reputation for cunning that echoes through folklore worldwide, which small omnivorous canid lives on every continent except Antarctica?
One of Maxwell's equations, this application of the divergence theorem connects electric charge distribution to the electric field it creates. Which one is it?
Gauss's law: Foundational law of electromagnetism relating electric field and charge distributions.
Google's mailbox provider is the largest email service in the world. Roughly how many users does it have?
Gmail is a mailbox provider by Google and the largest email service worldwide, with 1.8 billion users.
Also nicknamed the millionfish, this livebearing freshwater fish is one of the world's most popular aquarium species — which fish?
This medical term describes red blood cells rupturing and spilling their contents into the plasma — a process triggered by bacterial toxins or even intense exercise. What is it?
Hemolysis: Rupturing of red blood cells and release of their contents. Hemolysis may occur in vivo or in vitro.

The only birds whose first two neck vertebrae are fused together, these Old World birds have a long down-curved bill sometimes topped with a bony casque, and share an ecological niche with toucans in the Americas — which birds?
Hornbill: Family of birds. The family is omnivorous, feeding on fruit and small animals.
Marked in its severe stage by hallucinations and paradoxical undressing, which condition is defined as a body core temperature below 35 degrees Celsius?
Hypothermia: Human body core temperature below 35 °C (95 °F)
Named after the Greek word for rainbow because its compounds show so many colors, this brittle silvery-white metal is the second-densest element found in nature — what is it?
Iridium: Chemical element with atomic number 77 (Ir)
With Emmanuelle Charpentier, this Berkeley biochemist proposed in 2012 that CRISPR-Cas9 could edit genomes — work that won them the 2020 Nobel in Chemistry; who is she?
Jennifer Doudna: American biochemist and Nobel laureate (born 1964)
A genus of roughly 125 succulent species native mostly to Madagascar, one of its members became one of the first plants ever sent into space, aboard a Soviet resupply mission in 1979 — which genus?
Kalanchoe: Genus of flowering plants in the stonecrop family.
With a toothed, funnel-like sucking mouth, this jawless fish's name may derive from Latin for 'stone licker,' and it's genetically closer to hagfish than to any jawed vertebrate — what is it?
Lamprey: Class of jawless fish. Lampreys (sometimes inaccurately called lamprey eels) are a group of jawless fish composing the order Petromyzontiformes, sole order in the class Petromyzontida.
Sometimes called the paleomammalian cortex, this set of brain structures — including the amygdala — governs emotion, motivation, and long-term memory — what is it called?
Limbic system: Set of brain structures involved in emotion and motivation. Its various components support a variety of functions including emotion, behavior, long-term memory, and olfaction.

This German fluid dynamicist built the mathematical foundations of subsonic aerodynamics, identifying the 'boundary layer' and lifting-line theory — and lent his name to a dimensionless number. Who was he?

Despite its fox-like markings, this leggy, reddish-coated canine of the South American savanna is neither a fox nor a close relative of more familiar canines, and it plays a key role dispersing fruit seeds — what is it?

This elephant-sized extinct genus of South American ground sloths, whose type species weighed up to four tonnes, was first identified from a fossil found on an Argentine riverbank in 1787 — which genus?
Megatherium: Genus of extinct ground sloth. The first (holotype) specimen of Megatherium americanum was discovered in 1787 on the bank of the Luján River in what is now northern Argentina.
Sold as Versed, this benzodiazepine sedates rather than knocks you out, can be sprayed up the nose or squirted in the cheek, and famously causes anterograde amnesia — which drug?
Midazolam: Benzodiazepine used for anesthesia and procedural sedation.
This rounded mound of fatty tissue overlies the junction where the two pubic bones meet — what is it?
Mons pubis: Rounded mass of fatty tissue found over the pubic symphysis.
Made by giving a paper loop a half-twist before joining the ends, this non-orientable surface first appeared in Roman mosaics — what is it called?
Möbius strip: Non-orientable surface with one edge.
A former director of Russia's FSB who later served as Security Council secretary, this close Putin ally played a key role in the decisions to annex Crimea and invade Ukraine — who is he?
Nikolai Patrushev: Russian politician and security officer (born 1951)

The type species that gives its name to the Oleaceae family of lilac, jasmine, and ash, this Mediterranean evergreen bears a fruit classed botanically as a drupe — like a cherry or peach — what is it?

Though isolated observations date back to the 6th century BC, this science's modern foundation is credited to Georges Cuvier's 1796 work demonstrating that species could go extinct — what field is this?
Paleontology: Study of past life through fossils.
Commonly called geraniums or storksbills, this genus of roughly 280 evergreen species was split from a related genus by a botanist in 1789 — which genus, native largely to southern Africa?
Pelargonium: Genus of plants. It includes about 280 species of perennials, succulents, and shrubs.
This colorless, highly toxic pnictogen hydride is pure when odorless, but technical samples reek of rotting fish — and impurities can make it burst into flame in air — what is it?
Named after a French mathematician and physicist, this materials-science measure captures how much a material bulges sideways when compressed lengthwise — what is it?
Poisson's ratio: Measure of material deformation perpendicular to loading.
Found just below the bladder with the urethra passing through it, this male-only gland acts like a muscle-driven switch between urination and ejaculation — which organ?
Prostate: Gland of the male reproductive system.
Its thick bark gets harvested every 9 to 12 years for wine-bottle stoppers and cricket-ball cores — what species of oak, native to southwest Europe and Africa, is this?
Quercus suber: Species of plant. Quercus suber, commonly called the cork oak, is a medium-sized, evergreen oak tree in the section Quercus sect.

This dimensionless ratio of inertial to viscous forces predicts whether fluid flow will be smooth and laminar or chaotic and turbulent, and is used everywhere from pipe flow to aircraft wings — what is it?
Reynolds number: Ratio of inertial to viscous forces acting on a liquid.
Also called baked-apple berry or Arctic berry, this amber-hued fruit resembling a blackberry grows wild across boreal forests and Arctic tundra — what's its scientific name?
Rubus chamaemorus: Species of flowering plant in the rose family.
This large, rainbow-plumed parrot native to the forests of Central and South America is the national bird of Honduras — what is it?
Scarlet macaw: Species of bird. Like its relative the blue-and-yellow macaw, the scarlet macaw is a popular bird in aviculture as a result of its striking plumage.
The first woman on Facebook's board, she turned the company profitable as its long-serving COO and founded LeanIn.Org — who is she?
In 1948, this Japanese engineer turned a wooden shack producing bicycle motors into a multinational car and motorcycle manufacturer — who is he?
Soichiro Honda: Japanese businessman. Soichiro Honda (本田 宗一郎, Honda Sōichirō; 17 November 1906 – 5 August 1991) was a Japanese engineer and industrialist.

An English dyer and astronomer, he was the first to systematically show, around 1729, that electricity could travel through metals — flipping the era's focus from mere static sparks to conduction. Who was he?
Stephen Gray (scientist): English physicist. Stephen Gray (December 1666 – February 1736) was an English dyer and astronomer who was the first to systematically experiment with electrical conduction.
Commonly known as fainting, this fast-onset, short-duration loss of consciousness and muscle strength is typically caused by a sudden drop in blood flow to the brain — what's the medical term?
Syncope (medicine): Transient loss of consciousness and postural tone.
Patented in 1953 and originally derived from Streptomyces bacteria, this antibiotic treats ailments from acne to cholera to plague by blocking bacterial protein production — which drug?
Tetracycline: Antibiotic. It is available in oral and topical formulations.
Home to more than 4,200 described species, this family of large crane flies can be identified by the length of their maxillary palps — what is it?
Tipulidae: Family of flies. There are more than 30 genera and 4,200 described species in Tipulidae, common and widespread throughout the world.
Element 74 boasts the highest melting point of any known element — a scorching 3,422 °C — and carries the symbol W from its German name. Which metal is it?
Tungsten: Chemical element with atomic number 74 (W)
Released from the posterior pituitary when body fluids get too concentrated, this hormone helps kidneys reabsorb water and may also influence pair bonding — what is it?
Vasopressin: Mammalian hormone released from the pituitary gland.
Nicknamed the 'cock-of-the-woods,' this ground-dwelling grouse is the largest of all its kind, with males growing to nearly twice the size of females — which bird?
Western capercaillie: Species of bird. The bird shows extreme sexual dimorphism, with males nearly twice the size of females.
Nicknamed the ZZ plant or eternity plant, this glossy-leaved houseplant genus native to eastern Africa is prized for being nearly impossible to kill — name the genus?
Zamioculcas: Species of plant. Zamioculcas is a genus of flowering plants in the family Araceae, containing the single species Zamioculcas zamiifolia.
Xenon is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for xenon is Xe. Xenon is a chemical element; it has symbol Xe and atomic number 54.
Bismuth is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for bismuth is Bi. Bismuth is a chemical element; it has symbol Bi and atomic number 83.

In what year was Cher born?
Cher (SHAIR; legally mononymous; born Cheryl Sarkisian, May 20, 1946) is an American singer and actress.
In what year was Olga Kurylenko born?
Olga Kurylenko: Olga Kostyantynivna Kurylenko (born 14 November 1979) is a Ukrainian-born French actress and former model.
In what year was Gal Gadot born?
Gal Gadot (Hebrew: גל גדות, pronounced [ˈɡal ɡaˈdot]; born 30 April 1985) is an Israeli actress.
In what year was Lily-Rose Depp born?
Lily-Rose Depp: Lily-Rose Melody Depp (born May 27, 1999) is a French and American actress and singer.
In what year was Fran Drescher born?
Fran Drescher: Francine Joy Drescher (born September 30, 1957) is an American actress, writer, comedian, producer, and former trade union leader.
In what year was Chuck Norris born?
Chuck Norris: Carlos Ray "Chuck" Norris (March 10, 1940 – March 19, 2026) was an American martial artist, actor, screenwriter, and author.
In what year was Prabhas born?
Prabhas made his acting debut with the drama Eeswar (2002) and later attained his breakthrough with the action romance Varsham (2004).
In what year was George Lucas born?
George Lucas: George Walton Lucas Jr. (born May 14, 1944) is an American filmmaker and philanthropist.
In what year was Golshifteh Farahani born?
Golshifteh Farahani: Rahavard Farahani (Persian: رهاورد فراهانی; born 10 July 1983), known professionally as Golshifteh Farahani (گلشیفته فراهانی), is an Iranian actress.
In what year was Robert Redford born?
Robert Redford: Redford began his career on television in the late 1950s, appearing in anthology series such as Alfred Hitchcock Presents and The Twilight Zone.
In what year was James Caan born?
James Caan: James Edmund Caan ( KAHN; March 26, 1940 – July 6, 2022) was an American actor.
In what year did Roald Dahl die?
Roald Dahl: Dahl was born in Wales to affluent Norwegian immigrant parents, and lived for most of his life in England.
In what year was Dr. No first released?
Dr. No (film): No is a 1962 spy film and the first film in the James Bond series, starring Sean Connery as the fictional MI6 agent James Bond.
In what year was Asteroid City first released?
Asteroid City: The play is contexualised through a television documentary following the creation of the show itself, adding a layer of metatextuality.
In what year was Civil War first released?
Civil War (film): With a budget of $50 million, Civil War was A24's most expensive film at the time.
